restatement: Add a {{RAW}}...{{END_RAW}} block to the template resolver, done only in the lexer: after a tag whose trimmed content is exactly RAW, everything up to the first END_RAW tag becomes one ordinary Text token (not trimmed, CRLF turned into LF, no token when empty). The parser and interpreter stay untouched, so the block repeats in loops and vanishes in untaken branches like any other text. An unclosed RAW must throw the lexer's SyntaxError at the RAW tag's line and column, templates without RAW must behave exactly as before, and the README must gain one RAW section with an accurate example. No nesting, escapes or options.
brief_mismatch: c5 is marked verify: review and requires that the jest suite and the node:test suite pass, but the packet carries no test-run output and the reviewer may not run anything, so the 'suites pass' half of c5 cannot be judged here. Only 'jest suite files are untouched' is checkable: the visible diff touches no test file, and the 6 omitted paths are stated to be under docs/ephemeral/. Likewise c6 needs a person's confirmation of the README output, and no such record is in the packet. Separately, the project goal says 'correct for the n8n node', while the spec puts the n8n node file out of scope; if the node inspects the template text outside the lexer, the card cannot meet the cycle goal inside its own scope (see f1).
verification_plan: c1: confirm the RAW branch triggers only when the trimmed tag content is exactly RAW, and that the content is taken by position from the source up to the first END_RAW with no tag, variable or comment scanning in between.
c1: confirm exactly one Text token is emitted for the content and that the RAW and END_RAW tags themselves emit nothing; trace the rb-01 template by hand.
c2: confirm the token is a plain TokenType.TEXT with the same shape as other text tokens, so the unchanged parser and interpreter treat it as body text in FOR and IF; trace both rb-02 templates.
c3: confirm no trim is applied to the content, that CRLF is replaced by LF and nothing else is rewritten; then check whether anything downstream of the lexer trims or collapses text at render time.

c4: confirm that with no END_RAW the lexer throws its own SyntaxError with the RAW tag's start line and column (line 1, column 2 for 'a{{RAW}}b'), message 'Unclosed {{RAW}} block', hint 'Add {{END_RAW}}', and does not silently consume the rest.
c4 and rubric: confirm line and column are advanced correctly across the raw content, including newlines, so tokens and errors after a RAW block report correct positions.

c5 and rubric: confirm the new code is unreachable for templates without a RAW tag, that a stray END_RAW still gives the unknown-tag error, and that no other lexer path, token type or test file changed.
m1: confirm the diff touches only lexer.ts, README.md and docs/living/product/raw-block.md, with no parser, interpreter, Token or AST type change.
m2: confirm there is no nesting counter, no escape handling, and that 'RAW with arguments' is not accepted as an option form.
c6: evaluate the README example by hand against the lexer logic and compare with the printed output; confirm there is exactly one example.
Project goal: check whether any n8n-node feature that reads the template (variable detection, strict mode) could see the raw content as live syntax.

findings.title: Strict Mode / variable detection in the n8n node may still treat ${{name}} inside RAW as a required variable

serves.scenario: A prompt template holding a literal code sample such as {{RAW}}${{name}}{{END_RAW}} is run in the n8n node with Strict Mode on (the documented default) and no mapping for 'name'. If the node detects variables by scanning the template text rather than the lexer's tokens, it reports 'name' as missing and errors, so the template still cannot include tag-like text in the node. The detection code is not in the packet, so this is unverified.

findings.rubric: Goal-critical question 1 (everything between RAW and END_RAW comes out exactly as written); project goal 'correct for the n8n node'
findings.reproduction: In the n8n node, set Template to '{{RAW}}${{name}}{{END_RAW}}', leave Variable Mappings empty, keep Strict Mode on and enable Show Detected Variables. Expected: output '${{name}}', no error, and 'name' absent from detected_variables and missing_variables. Failure: a missing-variable error, or 'name' listed. If it fails, the smallest fix is to make detection ignore RAW spans, which needs a scope exception because the node file is out of scope.
evidence: doc:README.md (Node Configuration: 'Strict Mode — Error on missing variables (default: on)'; Output: detected_variables / missing_variables)
diff:nodes/TemplateResolver/lexer.ts (the change is lexer-only; no detection path is touched)
test:rb-01 a RAW block renders its content literally with no variables (goes through Lexer/Parser/Interpreter directly, bypassing the node's strict-mode path)

findings.title: Line and column tracking across multi-line raw content is not demonstrated

serves.scenario: scanRaw skips the content and closing tag with this.advance(closing.index) and this.advance(closing[0].length). The definition of advance is not in the packet. If advance(n) does not count newlines inside the skipped span, every token and error after a multi-line RAW block reports the wrong line and column, including a later unclosed RAW.

findings.rubric: Line and column tracking stays correct for tokens after a RAW block.
evidence: test:rb-04 an unclosed RAW block throws a SyntaxError at the RAW tag position (single line only, no preceding RAW block)
test:rb-03 RAW keeps leading and trailing spaces and turns CRLF into LF (checks value only, never line or column)

findings.title: Render-level preservation of leading/trailing whitespace and blank lines in raw text is untested

serves.scenario: c3 says the raw text is not trimmed, but the only rb-03 test stops at the lexer. The raw content is emitted as an ordinary Text token, so any whitespace handling the unchanged parser or interpreter applies to text (trimming block bodies, dropping newlines next to block tags, collapsing blank lines) would also apply to raw content. A multi-line code sample inside an IF or FOR body could then lose its leading newline or indentation. The parser and interpreter are not in the packet, so this is unverified.

findings.title: Closing-tag match allows only spaces and tabs inside the braces

serves.scenario: The spec says the closing tag may have inner spaces 'as other tags do'. Other tags are matched on their trimmed content, which presumably also tolerates a newline inside the braces. The regex /\{\{[ \t]*END_RAW[ \t]*\}\}/ does not, so '{{RAW}}x{{END_RAW\n}}' is reported as an unclosed RAW block. This is a polish-level inconsistency and no criterion fails on it.
